author: Ryan Hall
title: Alabama State Board of Education holds off on vote for social studies textbooks - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Hall ,
1 hours ago
MONTGOMERY, Ala. ( WIAT ) — The State Board of Education is delaying a vote on which social studies content should be recommended to schools.
Goo Goo Dolls to perform at The Wharf Last year, the state board of education adopted a course of study for history in the state. With those new standards comes new textbooks. Board members have different takes on what book best serves Alabama students.
A committee at the State Board of Education reviews potential textbooks for schools to use and then recommends a selection to board members. Dr. Wayne Reynolds, of Athens, said he is concerned about the content of those recommendations and the ability of the public to review the books before adoption.
He said social studies textbooks can have ramifications when it comes to politics and bias.
“The bigger markets, which tend to be more California and Texas and New York, guide what the writers are writing and what they include,” said Dr. Reynolds. “So, it’s not always easy for us to get the kind of textbooks that we want in Alabama.”
But, Dr. Yvette Richardson, of Fairfield, said the recommended textbooks meet state standards.
“As a former teacher, principal, superintendent, and now in higher education, I don’t have any concerns because I feel that the committee has done its due diligence in looking at the standards,” she shared.
Richardson explained local boards can still purchase their own books that abide by those standards.
“That serves as a framework for school districts. Even though we send that out, there are some school districts locally who basically will go forward with supplemental texts and other textbooks that they’d like to have,” she said.
Reynolds said by delaying a vote, State Superintendent Dr. Eric Mackey is going to reevaluate concerns members have.
“The one thing the public can know is their state board members are very diligent in what we do to guard and safeguard our education systems. And textbooks are a foundational part of that,” Reynolds said.
Mobile man arrested after police chase, allegedly hitting vehicles: MPD The State Board of Education will meet Thursday for their monthly meeting, but a vote on recommending a social study textbook for schools is not on the docket. Dr. Reynolds said the matter will likely be discussed in January.
